messages:
liz: Quick sync — trying to settle who owns the scale-window semantics for Dedicated GPU pools. Control-plane (global policy) or operator (local fast reactions)?
arjun: my leaning: operator owns immediate admission/eviction for latency, control-plane owns economic & SLA policy. keep surfaces tiny.
sam: agree w/ arjun. operator should have a small deterministic admission API: Admit(request) -> accepted|queued|preempt. control-plane pushes policy.
maria: +1. also need the telemetry contract so control-plane can compute cost/quality signals without peeking into tenant secrets. stats only.
kai: curious about race scenarios — operator might prewarm and then control-plane instructs scale-down. who wins? we need hysteresis rules.
arjun: propose rule: operator local decisions have a short-lived lease (e.g., 30s) after which control-plane reconciliation can override. prevents flip-flop.
liz: 30s seems reasonable as default. can we make it configurable per-pool? some latency-sensitive tenants want 5s.
sam: yes, expose lease_ttl in PoolSpec. control-plane validation ensures bounds [5s, 5m].
maria: telemetry: operator must emit per-pool headroom, inflight, prewarm credits, and last-policy-version. no payloads.
kai: what about admission windows for burst lanes? operator should accept guaranteed requests even if predictive capacity is running. control-plane marks guaranteed vs best-effort.
arjun: exactly — annotate requests with tier: guaranteed|standard|best_effort. operator enforces strict ordering for guaranteed.
liz: small DSL sketch for policy (very rough):
```
policy {
  pool_selector: "gpu:dense-v2"
  bounds {
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 40
  }
  lease_ttl_seconds: 30
  burst_lane: { reserved_percent: 10 }
}
```
sam: nice. also include a version hash and monotonic generation id so operator can detect drift.
infra-bot: build/check — policy-schema v0.3 validated, minor lint warnings. :white_check_mark:
maria: one more tradeoff: where to compute predictive signals (arrival rate forecasts)? doing it centrally simplifies model management but increases control-plane load. doing it at operator keeps data local but proliferates models.
arjun: hybrid — control-plane computes long-horizon forecasts and publishes compact signals (forecast_1m, forecast_5m, variance). operator runs a tiny local smoother for noise.
kai: failure modes: operator crash during canary -> control-plane must not keep sending scale commands that assume operator state. we need heartbeat + leader-elected operator for each shard.
liz: action items: arjun + sam to draft Admit API + lease semantics, maria to detail telemetry contract, kai to write failure-mode checklist. i'll compile into an RFC follow-up next week.
sam: will add a simple JSON schema for the policy snippet above.
arjun: i'll prototype operator-side lease machinery and submit a PoC to the dev environment.
maria: I'll stub Prometheus metrics and a README for the signals.
infra-bot: reminder — weekly arch sync Thu 10am.
liz: thanks all. moving to #eng-runtime sync after lunch. :thumbsup:
